laneSummaries: LANE A — CALLER-FEE / INCENTIVE FUNCTIONS IN DEFI: 30 sources, 17 of them NEW paying-function finds beyond wave 1, all read at the source level (GitHub contents API on the protocol's own repo, or the protocol's own docs) rather than from memory. The single best discovery: **Curve's fee-collection stack is live on Gnosis** — `FeeCollector.collect()`, `FeeCollector.forward()` and `Hooker.act()` are all explicitly permissionless, all take a `_receiver: address = msg.sender`, and all pay a keeper fee that DUTCH-RAMPS from 0 up to 1% of the value moved, so the reward grows until somebody takes it. That is the exact "contract pays the caller more than the call costs" shape, on a chain where we have free slots, with zero capital. Gnosis: FeeCollector `0xBb7404F9965487a9DdE721B3A5F0F3CcfA9aa4C5`, Hooker `0xE898893ebAe7b75dc4cAB0fb16e24137309ff178`. Second-best, zero-capital, mainnet: `CrvDepositor.lockCurve()` — no arguments, no capital, mints the entire accrued `incentiveCrv` pool to msg.sender (I read the four lines that do it). Third: Ajna `RewardsManager.updateBucketExchangeRatesAndClaim()` pays 5% (`UPDATE_CLAIM_REWARD = 0.05e18`) of burn-derived rewards in AJNA to whoever refreshes bucket exchange rates in the 2-week window after a burn event. A whole sub-class of the Convex/Aura family that wave 1 missed: the *StakingProxy* `distribute()` / `distributeOther(token)` functions (0.25% `callIncentive`), which are separate contracts from `Booster.earmarkRewards`. Also new: StakeDAO `Strategy.harvest()` (claimIncentiveFee to msg.sender), Penpie `batchHarvestMarketRewards()`, Origin `Harvester.harvestAndSwap(strategy, rewardTo)` ("Can be called by anyone", live on Base), Olympus `Heart.beat()` (dutch-auctioned OHM keeper reward), Curve crvUSD `PegKeeperV2.update()`, Yield Yak `reinvest()`. TWO IMPORTANT TRAPS I found by reading code, not docs: the entire Impermax/Tarot autocompounder family AND PancakeSwap's CakeVault gate their caller fee behind `require(msg.sender == tx.origin)` / a `notContract` modifier — that is structurally incompatible with a sponsored relay (relay msg.sender is a contract), so their bounty is unreachable for a zero-balance wallet no matter how attractive the number looks. Killed with reasons: Compound Comet `absorb` (pays points, not tokens; the profit leg needs base-token capital), Aave/Ajna/Euler liquidations (capital), GMX v2 executeOrder (genuinely counterparty-funded, but ORDER_KEEPER is role-gated), Keep3r Network (requires bonded KP3R), Yearn v3 `report()` (onlyKeepers), Curve gauge `kick()` (permissionless but pays zero). Honest gap: I could not verify the *current dollar size* of any of these fees — every $/call figure would be a remembered number, so I state none. The next step is a read-only measurement pass on the Gnosis FeeCollector: call `fee(Epoch.COLLECT)` / `fee(Epoch.FORWARD)` and price the pending balance, which costs nothing and converts this whole lane from "shape confirmed" to "amount measured". Search budget note: the session's 200 WebSearch calls were already exhausted before this lane started, so every finding here came from GitHub source reads and direct doc fetches — which is stronger evidence anyway.

LANE B — Liquidations, oracle pokes and liveness bounties: HARD FINDING FIRST: almost every lending liquidation in this lane is CAPITAL-REQUIRED, not zero-capital. The liquidator must actually repay the borrower's debt to seize discounted collateral. The bonus (5-10%) is real and is genuine sponsorship (the borrower's collateral pays the caller more than the call costs), but ZERO at $0.00 cannot take those trades without a flash-loan + DEX route built first, and even then it needs a profitable swap path. I refuse to dress that as USE_NOW.

THE ONE TRUE ZERO-CAPITAL SHAPE I FOUND — Sky/MakerDAO Liquidation 2.0 keeper incentives. VERIFIED in the `dss` Clipper source: `coin = add(_tip, wmul(tab, _chip)); vat.suck(vow, kpr, coin);` — the protocol MINTS payment from the surplus buffer to `kpr`, an address the caller chooses. No capital, no repayment, no collateral handling. `Dog.bark(ilk, urn, kpr)` (start the auction) and `Clipper.redo(id, kpr)` (reset a stale auction) are both pure paid cranks: flat fee + % of tab, paid to whoever calls. This is exactly our proven shape (contract pays caller more than call costs) and is the single best target in Lane B. Downside: Ethereum mainnet, heavily contested, and `redo` only pays when the remaining auction exceeds `chost` — which explicitly EXCLUDES dust, cutting against our dust edge. Second best: Inverse Finance FiRM `forceReplenish()` — VERIFIED "anyone can call", caller takes 10% of the replenishment cost; a liveness bounty, not a liquidation.

FREE-SLOT CHAINS: I verified two real ones. Aave V3 Gnosis is live (POOL `0xb50201558B00496A145fE76f7424749556E326D8`, read from the bgd-labs address book), and Morpho Blue is live on Unichain (`0x8f5ae9CddB9f68de460C77730b018Ae7E04a140A`) and Base (`0xBBBBBbbBBb9cC5e90e3b3Af64bdAF62C37EEFFCb`). Ajna is on both Gnosis and Base. `AaveV3Unichain.sol` 404s in the address book — I did NOT confirm an Aave Unichain market and am not claiming one.

ORACLE POKES ARE A DEAD LANE — this is the most useful negative in the sweep. Pyth Express Relay, the obvious answer, was WOUND DOWN by governance OP-PIP-124 in July 2026; the contracts and SDKs are being retired. API3's OEV auctions are explicitly closed: "OEV updates are possible only for the Api3 partnered searchers and not the general public." UMA's oracle needs bonds everywhere and `settle()` pays nothing. Anyone pitching "get paid to poke oracles" in 2026 is selling a 2023 map.

OTHER VERIFIED NEGATIVES worth the ink: Compound III `absorb()` is permissionless AND pays nothing — only a `liquidatorPoints` tally with "in the future, they could be compensated via governance". Gains Network retired its NFT bot role to a Chainlink oracle network. Avantis "runs its own relayer, so no third-party keeper". Extra Finance's liquidation bot is team-operated and not yet open-sourced. Four plausible-looking leads, four closed doors, all confirmed from primary docs.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY, marked honestly as LEAD: Curve crvUSD `PegKeeper.update()` caller share (every doc URL 404'd — this is the highest-value unverified item and should be re-checked against the Vyper source, since a % of arb profit to any caller would be a second true zero-capital crank), Silo Finance, and Ionic (docs host threw a TLS error; it also suffered a prior exploit).

METHOD NOTE / EVIDENCE CAVEAT: WebSearch hit its 200-call session cap on my second query, so this lane was built almost entirely from direct WebFetch against primary docs, `llms-full.txt` corpora and raw GitHub source — which is stronger evidence than search snippets, but it means my coverage is biased toward protocols whose doc URLs I could guess correctly. Absence from this list is not evidence of absence. I did NOT read current on-chain values for Maker's `tip`/`chip` governance params, so the actual $/call is UNMEASURED — that is the one number that decides whether this lane is worth building, and it should be read from the chain before any code is written.

LANE C — Gnosis + Unichain payable sources: The sweep found nothing on these two chains because it was looking for the wrong shape. Both chains DO have payers — I verified them by eth_call against public RPCs (Gnosis chainId 0x64, Unichain 0x82), not from docs.

THE HEADLINE FIND: PoolTogether V5 is live and actively drawing on Gnosis (PrizePool 0x0c08...120f, draw 692 awarded / 693 open). Its Claimer pays whoever claims prizes ON BEHALF OF WINNERS up to 10% of the prize (maxFeePortionOfPrize = 0.1e18, VERIFIED). Measured prize sizes right now: tier0 = 5,490.62 xDAI (max claim fee 549 xDAI), tier1 = 107.51 xDAI (10.75), tier2 = 17.31 (1.73), tier3 = 2.37 (0.24). Zero capital, permissionless, pure caller fee, paid in WXDAI. This is exactly ZERO's proven shape and it is on a chain where we have 5/5 free relay slots.

THE ENABLER: SparkLend on Gnosis (Pool 0x2Dae...07e0) has FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL = 0 — VERIFIED on-chain. Free flash loans on Gnosis mean EVERY Gnosis liquidation becomes a zero-capital trade. That converts $20.3M of Aave V3 Gnosis debt and $14.6M of RealT RMM debt from "needs capital" into "needs gas we don't pay".

MEASURED LIQUIDATION BONUSES (read from each pool's config bitmap, not remembered):
- Aave V3 Gnosis: GNO 10%, WETH 6%, wstETH 6%, WXDAI/USDC.e/sDAI 5%. 9 reserves, $20.3M borrowed.
- SparkLend Gnosis: GNO 12%, wstETH 8%, sDAI 6%, WXDAI/WETH 5%.
- Euler V2 Unichain: maxLiquidationDiscount() = 1500 = 15% on eWETH-1 and ewstETH-1. 50 vaults, $1.35M borrowed.
- Morpho Blue Unichain: live, $571k borrowed, LIF ~1.05, and Morpho's own flashLoan is fee-free.

THE WILDCARD: Olas Mech Marketplace on Gnosis (0x4554...e329) is a live machine-to-machine paid work market — VERIFIED numTotalRequests = 2,235,409 and numUndeliveredRequests = 199,995. Requesters prepay a BalanceTracker; mechs deliver AI work and are paid per request in native xDAI/OLAS/USDC. No KYC, no captcha. The only gate is owning an Olas ServiceRegistry serviceId (registry VERIFIED live, 3,787 services minted). Worth a dedicated spike — it is the only non-liquidation income shape I found on these chains.

HONEST NEGATIVES: I rejected 9 candidates outright. The AMMs on Gnosis (Honeyswap, Swapr, Sushi, Balancer V2, Uniswap V3) and Curve's Gnosis ChildGaugeFactory (VERIFIED live) pay callers nothing — fee withdrawal is governance-gated. Uniswap V4's PoolManager on Unichain is live but its protocolFeeController is 0x0 and controller-only. Bunni V2's rebalancing, which looked like the ideal v4-hook caller incentive, is restricted to a governance whitelist of solvers. CoW solvers, Kleros jurors, Seer/Reality.eth answerers and Gnosis validators all require bonded capital and/or DAO approval.

CAVEAT I WILL NOT DRESS UP: PoolTogether's DrawManager rewards are currently ~0 — startDrawReward() and finishDrawReward() both read 0 and the PrizePool reserve() is 26,889 wei (dust). The draw-auction mechanism is real but is not paying right now. The Claimer fee is the live one, because it comes out of the prizes themselves, not the reserve. Also, the claim fee is a 6-hour Dutch auction (timeToReachMaxFee = 21600s), so 10% is the ceiling, not the expectation — competing bots claim earlier at lower fees.

NEXT ACTION: point ZERO at the PoolTogether Gnosis Claimer first. It needs no capital, no flash loan, no swap route, and no price oracle — just "find winners, call claimPrizes, collect WXDAI". Everything else on this list needs a flash-loan + swap leg built first.

LANE D — Intent / solver architectures where someone else executes: Hard finding: Lane D is almost entirely a MIRAGE for a $0 wallet, and I want that stated before the list. Intent protocols do not create money — they relocate the gas cost onto a solver who then charges it back inside the price. Every "gasless swap" I fetched (CoW, 1inch Fusion, 0x Gasless, LI.FI/Squid/Symbiosis, Mayan) recovers gas from the token being traded. Per the brief's own rule ("if the user ultimately pays, REJECT"), that is not sponsorship. It is still operationally important for a different reason, so I kept it as a rail rather than income: ZERO can sign a CoW/Permit2 order and move or sell any ERC-20 it ever earns WITHOUT EVER HOLDING ETH. That solves ZERO's real structural bug — Lane A keeper fees land as tokens on a wallet with no gas to spend them. Treat that as the lane's actual deliverable.

On the other side of the book — can ZERO BE the solver? Three gates, and only one protocol clears all three. (1) Permission: CoW needs passports + an onboarding call + a bonding pool (verified, machine-only FAIL); 1inch Fusion needs staked 1INCH; Hashflow/Bebop need MM onboarding; Everclear and Relay use their OWN first-party inventory. UniswapX is the exception — Uniswap's own docs say non-exclusive fillers are "permissionless, no vetting". (2) Inventory: rejected everywhere it is required (Across relayers hold token balances, Mayan drivers "use liquidity they already hold", deBridge takers front capital). UniswapX again is the exception, because an executor contract can source the output atomically from an AMM in the same transaction — no float. (3) Gas: this is where the lane dies. UniswapX Priority Orders run a priority-fee auction, and the FILLER pays the priority fee in native ETH out of its own EOA. Nobody sponsors that. So the one permissionless, inventory-free, tiny-order-friendly venue still needs ZERO to hold ~$2–5 of ETH on Unichain, and Lane D contains no mechanism to get it there.

Net: 0 USE_NOW revenue sources. 1 USE_NOW rail (gasless order signing as ZERO's token-exit path). The best real income candidate is UniswapX PriorityOrderReactor on Unichain (chain 130 — one of our free-slot chains, reactor 0x00000006021a6Bce796be7ba509BBBA71e956e37), permissionless and inventory-free, blocked only on a few dollars of gas. Second-best is CoW partner fee (appData partnerFee: any recipient address, 0 capital, 0 inventory, weekly payout ≥0.001 WETH) — but that is a DISTRIBUTION problem wearing an intent costume: it pays per unit of order flow we route, and we have no order flow. Same shape as THORChain affiliate fees and LI.FI integrator fees. I flagged those honestly rather than dressing them as mechanics.

Search budget note: the session's 200 WebSearch calls were exhausted early (by earlier waves), so everything below was researched via direct WebFetch of primary docs. 10 entries are VERIFIED from fetched docs; the rest are explicitly marked verified=false / INFERRED and should not be treated as measurements.

LANE E — Agent payment rails and machine-auth work markets: Measured, not remembered: I probed six x402 facilitator endpoints live and read the Gnosis chain directly. Headline: the seller side of x402 is genuinely wallet-only and gas-sponsored, and PayAI is the best non-Coinbase instance of it — no API key, no signup, `/supported` and `/discovery/resources` both answered 200 for me, the latter returning 100 currently-listed paid resources with today's timestamp (2026-08-13). That is the one rail here ZERO can join with a signature and zero dollars. Second: I found a live machine-only work market on Gnosis, our free-slot chain — the Olas legacy AgentMech at 0x77af31De…A786a emitted 4,785 events in the last 50,000 blocks with the most recent ~7.7h before head, requesters paying per delivered AI request. Notably the NEW MechMarketplace v2 (0xE035dc…e3bd) has code but ZERO logs in 200,000 blocks — deployed and idle, so route at the legacy contract, not the shiny one. Honest negatives worth as much as the positives: I checked every live facilitator for our free-slot chains and NONE support Gnosis (100) or Unichain (130) — x402 and our free slots do not overlap, so stop planning that pairing. The public x402.org facilitator is testnet-only (base-sepolia, Solana devnet, Algorand/Aptos/Stellar/Hedera testnets) and cannot carry revenue. thirdweb settles "using your own server wallet" — that is us paying gas, not sponsorship, plus a secret-key gate. Nevermined wants an API key and takes 1–2%. UMA proposing is dead for us twice over: $750 bond and a ~37-address whitelist since Managed OO V2. The MCP marketplaces are a graveyard for our constraints — Smithery charges creators $30/mo and pays $0, Glama's monetization is not live, and MCPize's 80% share pays out via Stripe (hard-banned). ERC-8004 is real and permissionless but pays nothing: the EIP says outright that "payments are orthogonal to this protocol", and independent research (arXiv 2606.26028) found only 3–15% of registrations expose a live endpoint — it is identity substrate, not income. One quiet find: PayAI supports skale-base, a natively zero-gas mainnet, which is sponsorship by construction rather than by somebody's goodwill.
